validity.recommendation: Add 'Assam Natural Gas Pipeline' to OtherEnglishNames -- that is PNGRB's current official title for this exact AGCL asset (105 km authorised, 107 km operating, 2.4 MMSCMD, entry #17 of the Operational Common Carrier table). PNGRB ALSO lists a completely separate, unrelated 8 km 'Assam Regional Network' owned by GAIL (authorised 04.11.2009, capacity 2.5 MMSCMD, entry #1, currently supplying 0.0 MMSCMD) -- GEM's title for P0906 collides with that GAIL entity's name, which is a real duplicate-flagging trap for future researchers (it tripped me on first pass). The two are not the same pipe: different owner, different length (8 km vs ~105 km), different diameter profile. No action needed beyond the alias -- do not merge/rename P0906 to match either PNGRB label, since GEM's title is an established identifier.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently of GEM. Assam Gas Company Ltd (AGCL), 100% Assam-government owned, is a real, currently operating gas transporter headquartered in Duliajan, Dibrugarh district -- corroborated by (1) PNGRB's own May-2026 line-wise NGPL register, which lists 'Assam Natural Gas Pipeline / AGCL' under both the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE table (authorised 20.12.2013, 105 km authorised, 107 km operating, 2.4 MMSCMD authorised+design capacity, 1.5 MMSCMD supplied, 60.4% utilisation) and the Regulation-17 detail table (same entity, sector breakdown: 0.75 power, 0.09 fertiliser, 0.59 petrochem/refineries, 0.03 iron&steel MMSCMD); and (2) three independent company-profile/government sources (indiamart.com, mysarkarinaukri.com, and the Assam state government's Industries & Commerce department page) that all describe AGCL as an active gas transporter with a c. 900-1,000 km steel pipeline network across upper-Assam districts including both Golaghat and Tinsukia -- matching GEM's recorded StartPrefecture/District (Golaghat) and EndPrefecture/District (Tinsukia) exactly. CLASSIFICATION: transmission is correct -- this is the PNGRB-declared common-carrier (Section-42/Regulation-17) trunk portion of AGCL's system, not a CGD distribution network. DUPLICATE CHECK vs the 35-pipeline India-gas roster and vs the wider PNGRB register: NOT a duplicate of any roster row. It superficially resembles GAIL's other GEM-tracked 'Regional Gas Network' rows (P0904 Agartala, P0923 Gujarat, P0943 Mumbai, P0911 Cauvery) which all trace to GAIL-owned PNGRB 'Regional Network' entities -- but P0906's owner (Assam Gas Co Ltd, not GAIL) and its length/capacity (104.73 km / 2.43 MMSCMD) match PNGRB's separate AGCL-owned 'Assam Natural Gas Pipeline' entity (105 km / 2.4 MMSCMD), not PNGRB's GAIL-owned 8 km 'Assam Regional Network' entity -- see attribution recommendation above. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 = Assam Gas Co Ltd 100% is correct and independently confirmed (AGCL is explicitly the listed PNGRB entity, and all three company-profile sources identify AGCL as sole operator). Fuel=Gas trivially correct. SPEC: LengthKnown 104.73 km vs PNGRB's current 105 km authorised (107 km operating) -- a sub-1% variance consistent with reading an earlier/more-precise PNGRB edition (wiki cites 'Retrieved 2023-07-12'); not a material error. Capacity 2.43 vs PNGRB's current 2.4 MMSCMD authorised/design capacity -- same story, immaterial (1.25%) variance, most likely stale-edition drift per the orchestrator's documented MMSCMD-formula pattern, not a unit or entity error. StartYear1=1967 is independently confirmed by three sources as AGCL's actual first gas-transportation year (first delivery to Namrup Thermal Power Station) -- correctly NOT sourced from the 2013 PNGRB authorisation date, which per the India playbook would have been a dating error. Diameter (350, 400, 500, 800 mm) sits inside AGCL's company-wide stated steel-pipe diameter range (50-800 mm per indiamart) but I could NOT independently verify that these four specific values apply to this exact 104.73 km declared segment -- the original citing source (assamgas.org/pdf/pipeline.pdf, an upper-Assam CGD network map) is now dead (the site migrated to a React SPA that serves the index shell for every path, including old PDF URLs -- confirmed via curl, HTTP 200 but no PDF, no 'Assam' or diameter text). Left as an unverified-but-plausible caveat rather than a hard spec concern. NOTE ON PNGRB PDF CITATION: url_verifier.py returns 'FAIL ... missing expected: Assam' on the PNGRB PDF -- this is the documented large-PDF false negative (per orchestrator brief); I downloaded it directly and ran pdftotext -layout locally, confirming the exact rows quoted above verbatim.

fills.researcher_notes: PNGRB's May-2026 NGPL register lists 'Assam Natural Gas Pipeline / AGCL' (105 km authorised / 107 km operating, 60.4% capacity utilisation) in the OPERATIONAL COMMON CARRIER PIPELINE table -- confirms currently operating. url_verifier gives a false-negative on this large PDF (documented issue); confirmed the match locally via pdftotext -layout.
Listed as a Natural Gas Pipeline (NGPL) in PNGRB's register; trivially correct.

PNGRB authorises this as a Section-42/Regulation-17 common-carrier natural gas transmission pipeline, distinct from AGCL's much larger CGD-style distribution network (900-1,000 km of steel + PE pipe) that reaches individual customers -- transmission classification is correct for the declared 105 km asset.

Two independent company-profile sources both state AGCL 'started in the year 1967 with supply of natural gas to Namrup Thermal Power Station' -- matches StartYear1 exactly. This is the actual first-gas year, not the 2013 PNGRB authorisation date (which would be the wrong field to source it from).

PNGRB's current edition shows 2.4 MMSCMD authorised/design capacity for this exact entity (AGCL, 105 km) -- a 0.03 MMSCMD (1.25%) variance from GEM's 2.43, consistent with the sheet having been sourced from an earlier PNGRB edition (wiki cites 'Retrieved 2023-07-12') rather than a unit or entity error. Single-source spec match -> medium tier; flagging the small variance rather than silently passing it, per corroboration rules.

PNGRB's current edition shows 105 km authorised length (107 km operating length -- the line has been extended slightly past its authorised length) for this entity. GEM's 104.73 km is a sub-1% variance from the rounded 105 km figure, consistent with an earlier/more-precise PNGRB edition rather than an error. Single-source match -> medium tier.

Could not independently verify these four specific diameter values for this exact 104.73 km segment. AGCL's company-wide steel-pipe diameter range is reported as 50-800 mm (indiamart.com) which is CONSISTENT with but does not confirm this precise set. The original citing source on gem.wiki (assamgas.org/pdf/pipeline.pdf, an upper-Assam CGD network map) is now dead: the site migrated to a React SPA that returns the index-page shell (HTTP 200, no PDF content, no 'Assam' or diameter text) for every legacy path I tried, including the Citizens' Charter PDFs. Leaving unref'd rather than pairing a weak/inexact source -- do not delete the existing value, it is plausible and within the confirmed range.

Two independent company-profile sources both list Golaghat and Tinsukia among the districts AGCL's pipeline network serves/passes through in upper Assam, corroborating GEM's recorded start (Golaghat) and end (Tinsukia) districts. Neither source states a definitive directional start/end point, but both confirm the two named districts sit on AGCL's single corridor alongside Jorhat/Sivasagar/Dibrugarh.

PNGRB's register lists 'AGCL' as the sole entity for this exact pipeline; indiamart.com independently confirms Assam Gas Company Ltd as the operating company. 100% ownership is consistent with AGCL being a wholly Assam-government-owned corporation with no reported joint ownership of this asset.

summary: P0906 (Assam Regional Gas Network / AGCL) is real and correctly classified as an operating transmission pipeline; length/capacity/start-year/owner/location all independently corroborated (PNGRB register + 3 company/govt sources), with only minor caveats: length/capacity show <1.5% variance vs the current PNGRB edition (stale-edition drift, not error), Diameter is plausible but unverifiable at this precision (source PDF now dead), and the GEM title collides in name only (not substance) with a separate, unrelated 8 km GAIL-owned 'Assam Regional Network' also in PNGRB's register -- recommend an OtherEnglishNames alias to head off future false duplicate flags.
